title: Ablaut Twin-Words (Hangváltakozó ikerszók) and Movement Reduplication

sections.title: Vowel Alternation in Hungarian Expressive Compounds
sections.content: You know twin-words and vowel alternation (*gizgaz*, *limlom*) from B2 Unit 67; here are more twin-words, with two kinds of ending. Many twin-words have vowel alternation (*izeg-mozog*: i-o; *mendemonda*: e-o); others rhyme (*irul-pirul*, *tarka-barka*). They reflect restless motion, colorful diversity, hesitation, or fluctuating states.

sections.title: Separable Motion Verbs: Izeg-mozog and Irul-pirul
sections.content: Unlike nominal compounds, verbal twin-words like 'izeg-mozog' (to fidget restlessly) or 'irul-pirul' (to blush with embarrassment) inflect across both elements in finite forms: 'izeg-mozog', 'izgett-mozgott'. Meanwhile, nominal compounds like 'mendemonda' (rumour, gossip) and adjectives like 'tarka-barka' (motley/kaleidoscopic) inflect only at the end.

sections.title: Common Ablaut Twin-Words and Motion Predicates
rows: A kisgyerek izeg-mozog a székben a hosszú táncelőadás alatt.
The toddler fidgets restlessly in the chair during the long dance performance.
A lány irult-pirult, amikor a legjobb legény hívta el táncolni.
The girl blushed with modesty when the finest lad asked her to dance.
Ne higgy a mendemondáknak a zenekar feloszlásáról!
Do not believe the unfounded rumors about the band breaking up!
A sokféle viselet tarka-barka forgataggá varázsolta a táncparkettet.
The diverse costumes turned the dance floor into a motley, swirling crowd.

items.spanish: A táncházban annyi fiatal gyűlt össze, hogy a teremben szinte mindenki izgett-mozgott a ritmusra.
items.english: So many young people gathered in the dance house that almost everyone in the room fidgeted and swayed to the rhythm.

items.spanish: Mindenféle alaptalan mendemonda terjedt arról, hogy bezár a táncház.
items.english: All sorts of baseless rumours spread that the dance house was closing.

items.spanish: A kalotaszegi és széki szoknyák tarka-barka kavalkádja lenyűgözte a külföldi látogatókat.
items.english: The motley cavalcade of Kalotaszeg and Szék skirts enchanted the foreign visitors.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Remember: in the past tense of 'izeg-mozog', both halves take past-tense endings: 'izgett-mozgott' (never 'izeg-mozgott'). In contrast, 'tarka-barka' is an adjective and takes suffixes only on the second stem: 'tarka-barkák'.
